title: Isao's close-up frames his face, not his legs; the comms card sits above the radar so the landing-site triangles show
context: Checking the story-world suite's own screenshots after the held-faces batch: the isaoTalk close-up put the camera between Isao's legs and the rocket with no face in frame, and the panel still carried the previous line (quiver_cleared) because briefs queue one deep; at the expedition beat the game's comms card sat over the radar, hiding the amber landing-site triangles the owner asked for.
outcome: The close-up camera now stands along Isao's own forward (the model's +Z, flattened to the tangent plane), level with the LED panel and one to two drone-sizes out, looking at the face; the queued line is cleared as the shot starts so 'They talk in vibration.' is the first thing on the panel. #td-brief now sits above the radar using the same sizing rule td-tab applies to the disc (min(240px, 32vmin) at 14 px on desktop; min(138px, 23vmin) at 700 px and narrower). Landing plumes verified in the story lab capture: the flames leave from under the base.
alternatives: Move the radar instead of the comms card: rejected, the radar's corner is a long-standing placement other overlays anchor to; the card is the newcomer.
evidence: artifacts/browser/story-world-isao-talk.png and story-world-expedition.png from the story-world suite; the story lab landing capture.
